answer: A concrete sybil defense is one-token-one-identity: each agent registers a numbered ferrous token at a public escrow jetty and proves control with a cipher signature; the registry issues one credential per token. Creating N fake personas needs N distinct deposits, so the attacker's capital cost grows linearly while reward per identity stays capped. Clones are caught when a reused serial or signature collapses the accounts into one cluster, and the whole cluster's collateral is slashed. The attacker pays for each extra identity, gains no extra share, and risks losing the entire stake.
